chunks: They swear oaths to you so that you may be pleased with them. If you are pleased with them, then God is not pleased with the disobedient people.

key_terms.الْفَاسِقِينَ: The disobedient / those who transgress boundaries
key_terms.لِتَرْضَوْا: So that you may be pleased

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between human acceptance and divine acceptance of hypocrites?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the political and spiritual duplicity of the Hypocrites (Munafiqun) who sought to ingratiate themselves with the early Muslim community through superficial oaths. It establishes that divine acceptance is contingent upon inner sincerity rather than external validation by the believers, marking the 'Fasiqun' as those whose outward piety masks internal corruption. This distinction underscores the Shia emphasis on the alignment of the heart with the word, a key criterion for true faith.
